biodiversity_overview.text: 15,803 GBIF occurrence records for 92 tracked species are attributed to Odisha, spanning 1902-2026.
15,383 of these records (97.3%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 27, Mammalia 16, Magnoliopsida 14, Actinopterygii 13, Testudines 8, Squamata 7, Amphibia 4, Crocodylia 1, Elasmobranchii 1, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 12 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU), Tiger (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (3,419), Indian Cuckoo-shrike (1,272), Indian Golden Oriole (1,074), Indian Pond-heron (1,064), Indian Roller (949).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 236 in 2016 to 494 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.17% of Odisha's area (21 areas intersect the state).
18.5% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (2,839 of 15,383); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle (0.54), Indian Bandfish (0.52), Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Scad (0.48).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Odisha (equal-weight reference): cell near 19.875N 85.875E (overall rank 38, median rank across weightings 53); cell near 19.125N 83.625E (overall rank 78, median rank across weightings 98); cell near 19.875N 85.125E (overall rank 86, median rank across weightings 105).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 26,953 km2 (17.62% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

1,476.8 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (5.48% of the 2000 extent; 3.03% in 2015-2024, rank 7 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2023 (116.6 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.62% of land and population density is 305.7 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
28% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
